title: AuthGuard: bot defence for the ILIAS account-registration form
description:
ILIAS plugin that rejects automated submissions of the self-registration form and offers the same protection to other plugins that publish forms to anonymous visitors. Every submission has to pass, in order, a submit-timing check (a form submitted less than two seconds after it was shown is refused), a honeypot (a hidden decoy field that only scripts fill) and a challenge provider chosen by the administrator. By default (Altcha) that challenge is a proof-of-work solved in the background without a click, generated and verified on the ILIAS server, and no visitor data leaves the installation. The administrator can instead select an external provider: Google reCAPTCHA v2 or v3 (with a configurable score threshold), Cloudflare Turnstile, hCaptcha or Friendly Captcha (global or EU endpoint). External providers send data about the visitor to the vendor, so the privacy policy of the installation must name it. Visitors without JavaScript get an image CAPTCHA as a fallback. Other plugins protect their own forms through a documented form protection API.

ILIAS core shipped a CAPTCHA on the self-registration form up to ILIAS 7 and removed it in ILIAS 8 on the grounds that it no longer kept bots out. This plugin restores the protection as a user-interface hook plugin, without any change to the ILIAS core.

The default proof-of-work and the honeypot ask the visitor for nothing. The image CAPTCHA, shown only to visitors whose browser runs no scripts, is image-only and does not meet WCAG 2.1 success criterion 1.1.1; installations subject to EN 301 549 should provide an alternative registration route. The accessibility of each external provider is the vendor's statement and has not been audited for this plugin.

For ILIAS 10 (10.0 and later 10.x), PHP 8.2 or 8.3.
